Fit mixture regression models with different numbers of classes, and compare them

Source: R/mixture-regression-enumerate.R
enumerate_regressions.Rd

enumerate_regressions() fits mixture regression models with different numbers of latent classes and compares them. The same outcome model is fitted across the requested class counts, so that researchers can assess whether additional classes provide a useful representation of variation in outcome-predictor relationships. The outcome distribution, predictors, and other supplied model settings remain common across candidates.

For supported two-level models, the function can also vary the number of group classes and fit each requested combination of class counts. The resulting table brings together information criteria, classification measures, class sizes, convergence, and likelihood replication. Individual fitted models are retained for examination of their coefficients, predictions, and class assignments.

An optional parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test compares models with consecutive numbers of regression classes while holding the number of group classes fixed. This provides additional evidence about whether the improvement in likelihood supports the more complex specification.

Usage

enumerate_regressions(
  formula,
  data,
  n_classes = 1:4,
  n_group_classes = 1L,
  bootstrap = 0L,
  bootstrap_starts = 3L,
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula outcome ~ predictors. Factors, interactions and offset() are supported.

data

A data frame.

n_classes

Positive integer class counts to fit. Default 1:4.

n_group_classes

Positive integer group-class counts (two-level model; needs id in ...), crossed with n_classes. Default 1, no group classes.

bootstrap

Number of bootstrap replicates for the likelihood-ratio test of k - 1 against k classes. 0 (the default) skips the test. A positive number adds the blrt_ columns to the table; each replicate refits two models, so the run time grows with it. Not available with sampling weights.

bootstrap_starts

Random starts for each bootstrap refit. Default 3.

seed

Optional integer seed for the starts and the bootstrap; when given, the caller's random-number state is restored on exit.

...

Further arguments to mixture_regression(), used for every model:

  • family: "gaussian" (default), "binomial", "poisson", "negative_binomial" or "ordinal";

  • id and class_level: "observation" (default, a class per row) or "group" (a class per unit of id);

  • variance: "varying" (default) or "equal";

  • common, membership, random and the other model arguments;

  • n_starts, max_iter, tol and missing ("error" or "omit").

n_classes, n_group_classes and vcov_type are not accepted here: the class counts are this function's own arguments, and the models are fitted without a stored covariance matrix. A name that is not an argument of mixture_regression() is refused.

Value

An object of class latents_regression_enumeration. Its table (from as.data.frame(), summary() or get_results(x, "fit")) has one row per model, with these columns:

  • n_classes, n_group_classes, log_likelihood, n_parameters;

  • aic, bic, bic_rows (BIC with the number of rows as the sample size), sabic and icl: lower is better;

  • entropy: between 0 and 1, higher meaning clearer classification;

  • smallest_share: the proportion of the smallest class;

  • converged and n_best_replicated (the number of starts that reached the best log likelihood);

  • note: why a model could not be fitted; its other columns are NA;

  • best_bic: TRUE for the rows with the smallest reported BIC, without filtering on convergence;

  • with bootstrap > 0: blrt_statistic, blrt_p_value, blrt_replicates (the valid replicates), blrt_n_invalid (the failed, unconverged, separated or reversed-likelihood replicates) and blrt_flagged (a compatibility alias for blrt_n_invalid). The test of a row compares it with the row that has one class fewer. These columns are NA where the k - 1 or k class model is missing or failed, and the p-value is NA when the observed fits fail validation or fewer than half of the requested replicates are valid.

get_results(x, "model", n_classes = , n_group_classes = ) returns one fitted model (a latents_mixture_regression or latents_growth_mixture fit), get_results(x, "tree") the class tree and get_results(x, "all") the named list of the fit and tree tables; any other what raises latents_bad_argument. print() shows the main columns of the table. plot() draws AIC, BIC, SABIC and ICL across the classes (see plot_enumeration() for its other views, and plot_views(x) for the views a regression grid offers).

Details

The optional parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test compares k - 1 with k classes at a fixed number of group classes. Outcomes are simulated under the smaller model, and both models are refitted to each simulated dataset. The p-value is (1 + b) / (1 + V), where b is the number of valid replicate statistics at least as large as the observed statistic and V is the number of valid replicates.

A replicate is invalid if a refit fails, does not converge, produces a separation or degenerate random-effect covariance warning, or yields a negative likelihood-ratio statistic beyond numerical tolerance. The p-value uses valid replicates only. Both valid and invalid counts are reported, and latents_failed_replicates warns when any replicate is invalid. The p-value is NA when fewer than half of the requested replicates are valid. Excluding invalid replicates conditions the reference distribution on successful estimation and may affect calibration. Report the invalid proportion and examine the refit diagnostics when interpreting the test.

Interpretation

The best_bic column identifies the smallest reported BIC among the fitted candidates; it does not exclude unconverged fits. Model assessment should therefore consider convergence and likelihood replication alongside information criteria, class sizes, and the meaning of the estimated regression relationships. Bootstrap results also require attention to unsuccessful refits, whose exclusion can affect the test.

Conditions

A model whose fit raises latents_no_valid_start or latents_bad_data at some count has a row of NA values with the condition message in note (and print() says how many); when every model fails with the same latents_bad_data error (a column that does not exist), that error is raised instead. Other errors stop the enumeration. latents_bad_argument for invalid n_classes, n_group_classes, bootstrap or bootstrap_starts, for an invalid seed, for an argument in ... that mixture_regression() does not have, for n_classes, n_group_classes or vcov_type passed through ..., for a bootstrap test whose outcome is not a plain column name, and from get_results() for a model that is not in the grid or could not be fitted. latents_unsupported_weights for a bootstrap test with sampling weights. latents_failed_replicates is warned, naming the count, when some replicates are invalid (the p-value then uses the valid ones), and when the observed fits fail validation or fewer than half of the replicates are valid (the p-value is then NA).

Examples

classes <- enumerate_regressions(score ~ hours, data = study_hours,
                                 n_classes = 1:3, n_starts = 3, seed = 1)
classes
#> Mixture regression class enumeration
#> 
#>  n_classes n_group_classes log_likelihood n_parameters  bic  icl entropy
#>          1               1          -3245            3 6510 6510      NA
#>          2               1          -3144            7 6336 7031  0.4430
#>          3               1          -3133           11 6341 7271  0.5293
#>  smallest_share converged best_bic
#>         1.00000      TRUE    FALSE
#>         0.43587      TRUE     TRUE
#>         0.07512      TRUE    FALSE
#> 
#> One model: get_results(x, "model", n_classes = ).
get_results(classes, "model", n_classes = 2)
#> Mixture of gaussian regressions: 2 classes (one class per row)
#> score ~ hours
#> 900 rows | log likelihood -3144.0073 | BIC 6335.63 | entropy 0.443
#> Converged: TRUE | iterations: 49 | best likelihood reached by 2 of 2 completed starts (4 run)
#> 
#> Classes
#> 
#> Class    Share  Expected  Rows assigned  Avg. posterior  Residual SD
#> -------  -----  --------  -------------  --------------  -----------
#> Class 1  0.564    507.72            573           0.789         5.24
#> Class 2  0.436    392.28            327           0.829         6.89
#> 
#> Regression coefficients (95% CI)
#> 
#> Class    Term       Estimate          95% CI      p
#> -------  ---------  --------  --------------  -----
#> Class 1  Intercept     34.36  [32.95, 35.77]  <.001
#> Class 1  hours          4.57  [ 4.36,  4.77]  <.001
#> Class 2  Intercept     54.90  [52.76, 57.04]  <.001
#> Class 2  hours          0.81  [ 0.48,  1.14]  <.001
#> 
#> Every table: get_results(x, what = ), e.g. "classes", "membership", "fit", "assignments".
# \donttest{
# With the bootstrap likelihood-ratio test of one against two classes.
# `bootstrap` is small so the example runs quickly; use many more
# replicates for inference.
with_test <- enumerate_regressions(score ~ hours, data = study_hours,
                                   n_classes = 1:2, variance = "equal",
                                   n_starts = 3, seed = 1, bootstrap = 4)
as.data.frame(with_test)
#>   n_classes n_group_classes log_likelihood n_parameters      aic      bic
#> 1         1               1      -3244.958            3 6495.916 6510.323
#> 2         2               1      -3149.398            6 6310.797 6339.611
#>   bic_rows    sabic      icl   entropy smallest_share converged
#> 1 6510.323 6500.795 6510.323        NA        1.00000      TRUE
#> 2 6339.611 6320.556 7010.972 0.4619063        0.37308      TRUE
#>   n_best_replicated note best_bic blrt_statistic blrt_p_value blrt_replicates
#> 1                 4 <NA>    FALSE             NA           NA              NA
#> 2                 4 <NA>     TRUE        191.119          0.2               4
#>   blrt_n_invalid blrt_flagged
#> 1             NA           NA
#> 2              0            0
# }
